post.caption: Men's wedding rings were once considered odd. Fortune magazine said so in 1947, in a piece called Ring Twice. Men mostly wore signet and graduation rings instead, and in 1926 an ad campaign for men's engagement rings flopped. Many soldiers wore wedding rings in World War II to remember home, and a 1944 ad showed a soldier with a ring reading a letter. The jewelry industry promoted double ring weddings on radio and in schools. Jewelers called the idea the double ring service. Fortune counted double ring weddings rising from 15 to 80 percent. By the early 1950s a groom's ring was standard.
